title: Launch Assurance — Stakeholder Runbook, Escalation Paths & Snapshot Rollback Guides
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Create a single coordinated Launch Assurance artifact that operationalizes release blockers, snapshot-based rollback procedures, and templated communications for incidents and post-rollback notes. The goal is to give SRE, Support, Sales Ops and Eng a clear runbook to execute a fast, auditable rollback or mitigation with minimal customer disruption.
acceptance_criteria: A single runbook exists in Confluence with step-by-step rollback instructions for both Canary and Global rollouts
Communication templates (incident alert, rollback notify, postmortem link) are approved by Legal and Support and stored in the runbook
Rollback path exercises completed in staging with a successful snapshot restoration within the target RTO: 10 minutes for canary, 30 minutes for global
All rollback steps are automated where possible (scripts/terraform/helm) and linked from the runbook
On-call escalation matrix validated and pager duty policies updated to include PM launch lead and Sales Ops contact
tasks: Draft initial runbook outline and publish a draft to Confluence (owner: Avery)
Define snapshot and DB restore cadence with Platform team and document pre-conditions (owner: Marco Silva)
Create rollback automation scripts and PRs to runtime-repo (owner: ENG oncall)
Collect and finalize communication templates, get Legal and Support sign-off (owner: Priya)
Run tabletop exercise with SRE/Support/Sales Ops and capture gaps (owner: Avery)
Update Release Notes checklist to include rollback verification and comm templates (owner: Release Manager)
Schedule dry-run in staging during low-traffic window and record metrics (owner: Marco)
Add rollback indicators to Console dashboards and alerting (owner: Observability)
Post-launch 72-hour watch plan and owner assignments (owner: Product)
rollout_plan: 1) Canary release to 5% traffic for 2 hours with enhanced logging and tracing enabled
2) Monitor key SLOs and alerts for 60 minutes; if stable, ramp to 25% for 1 hour
3) Hold and review metrics with launch stakeholders at each ramp step
4) If no regressions, proceed to 100% and begin 72-hour watch
5) If high-severity signals appear during any step, invoke rollback decision ladder (see rollback_plan)
rollback_plan: Trigger conditions: sustained SLO degradation >20% for 15 minutes, critical error rate spike, or customer-reported severity=1 incidents
Step A - Canary rollback: disable traffic split, re-route to previous variant; if configured, restore service VM snapshot for canary pool
Step B - Global rollback: pause global traffic, revert runtime image tag and database snapshot to pre-release timestamp, run smoke suite
Step C - Post-rollback verification: run critical path synthetic tests, confirm KV cache and session consistency, validate with Support on key customer sessions
Execution roles: SRE executes infra rollback, Eng Runtime owns image revert PRs, Product signals customer comms and Sales Ops engagement
Audit: log all steps to the runbook audit table and attach PR links and Cloud Console snapshots
communication_templates: Incident Alert - Initial (subject: [INCIDENT] runtime-1.22 - Investigating elevated error rate): Please triage immediately. Impact: potential user-facing failures. Current hypothesis: model cache invalidation during rollout. Actions taken: rolled back canary to previous variant and monitoring. Next update in 15 minutes. Owners: Marco (SRE), Avery (Runtime), Priya (PM).

Rollback Notify (subject: [ROLLBACK] runtime-1.22 - Canary rollback executed): We executed a canary rollback at 14:32 UTC due to error-rate regression. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /chat. Customer impact: intermittent failures between 14:10-14:32 UTC. Remediation: canary restored to v1.21. Follow up: a post-rollback investigation will be scheduled. Contact Support for known customer queries.

Global Rollback Escalation (subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] runtime-1.22 - Global rollback initiated): Global rollback for runtime-1.22 commenced. Expected RTO: 30 minutes. Sales Ops and Enterprise Success notified for high-value customers. All customer-facing comms must be routed through Support template A. Postmortem: assigned to Eng Runtime and SRE; timeline will be published within 48 hours.

Postmortem Summary (subject: [POSTMORTEM] runtime-1.22 - Root cause and next steps): Summary of what happened, impact metrics, root cause analysis, mitigation plan, release hold duration, and owners. Include links to PRs, dashboards, and remediation tickets.
test_plan: Pre-launch: run automated canary smoke tests and synthetic traffic replay against staging snapshots
Nightly staging restore of a production snapshot to validate DB restore scripts
Tabletop: 1 hour simulation with SRE/Support/Sales Ops to walk through communication templates and decision ladder
Dry-run: execute full rollback in staging using the automation scripts and measure RTO/RPO
Post-rollback: validate log integrity and tracing spans are preserved across restore
risks: Database schema drift could make snapshot restores non-deterministic
Rollback may leave ephemeral caches in inconsistent state causing session anomalies
Communication templates may not be localized for non-English markets; increases support load
Automated rollback scripts could have insufficient permissions in Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
High-severity incidents during a major holiday could overload Support and delay communications
